AI Risk Description: Bias in automated credit scoring leading to discriminatory lending outcomes
Lack of transparency in AI decision-making affecting customer trust and regulatory compliance
Inadequate data governance causing training data quality issues and model drift
Unauthorized access to AI models or training datasets (model theft / IP leakage)
AI system producing inaccurate or harmful outputs in clinical diagnosis
Failure to maintain human oversight in high-risk AI decision loops
Third-party AI vendor non-compliance with EU AI Act or ISO 42001 requirements
Inadequate documentation of AI system lifecycle and version control
Privacy breach through AI model memorization of personal data (training data leakage)
AI system non-conformance with sector-specific regulations (FCA/MHRA/SRA)
Insufficient testing and validation before AI system deployment
Lack of continuous monitoring for AI system performance degradation
Inability to trace AI decision audit trail for regulatory investigation
Employee misuse of AI tools leading to unauthorized automated decisions
Failure to update AI risk register after significant system change or new regulation
